verdict.rationale: Bun documents a global cache that stores every package downloaded from the registry, and an install mode that never touches the network and installs only from that cache, with hardlinks into node_modules. Nothing in the evidence addresses prebuilt native binaries or avoiding source compilation. One commenter only believes Bun can run node-gyp for packages that need it. missing for 10: documented prebuilt-binary resolution for native addons, evidence that cached installs avoid compilation steps, independent hands-on corroboration of cache-based installs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install prebuilt binary packages from a cache instead of compiling from source

citations.quote: Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, or the path set by the `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.
Never touch the network (registry, tarball URLs, git); a required dependency that is not cached is an error
On Linux and Windows, Bun uses hardlinks to "copy" a module into a project's `node_modules` directory, so the contents of the package only exist in a single location on disk.
